newsitem.title: USA: Maryland seeks drought relief from Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Maryland seeks drought relief from Clinton.

text.p: Maryland Gov. Parris Glendening called on the Clinton administration Wednesday to grant disaster relief to state farmers suffering from a summer drought.

"The excessive heat and the prolonged dry spell in many key agricultural regions of the state...are costing Maryland farmers millions of dollars in losses," Glendening said in letters forwarded to President Clinton and U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman.
The governor said the state would conduct an assessement to determine which counties would be eligible for aid.

Preliminary surveys by the Maryland State Consolidated Farm Service Agency have shown losses of 25-50 percent for grain and soybeans, while pasture losses in some counties have been put at 80 percent.
Three counties -- Frederick, Carroll and Washington -- have been hit hardest by drought conditions.
Maryland farmers last qualified for disaster assistance during a severe drought in 1995. ((Philadelphia Bureau --
